licences.notes: Words as printed in the Peters vocal score: “Fate presto o cari amici” without a comma, giá (with the print's acute accent), finchè, quà, comediola, Don Alfonso's “s'avanzano” (the libretto has “si avanzano”) and “vista, o si vedrà” with the comma before the elided o.

licences.source: Edition Peters vocal score (Edition Peters Nr. 4474, plate 11446, edited by Georg Schünemann), pages 311–315, bars 1–65 of No. 31
licences.author: Kurt Soldan (1891–1946), piano reduction
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: the No. 31 Finale (671 bars) read in fourteen page ranges, sung lines and piano each by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the zoomed page by a judge, a separate sweep for dynamics and other marks, then checked bar by bar by eight fresh proofreaders (pages 311–317 clean). The German singing translation is left out. All the singers of this section have a staff throughout, with rests where the print leaves a staff out; singers who do not sing in this section are left out. The chorus (sopranos, altos, tenors and basses; servants and musicians) has a staff for each part and is heard with the piano; it has no role here. Where the print gives the basses no words, they sing the tenors' words. Cut from the one-file finale at bars 1–65: from the start of the finale (Allegro assai, C major) to the last bar before the Andante. The sopranos and altos print “pre-po-ria-mo” for prepariamo in bar 29; it is kept as printed. Playback tempo ♩ = 173 from René Jacobs's recording (harmonia mundi), 1:30.
